newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU maltsters seek more export licences.
newsitem.headline: EU maltsters seek more export licences.

text.p: European maltsters will be seeking more licences, despite the rush of applications which took exports to their normal annual 1.8 tonne million figure last week.
"We shall be holding talks with the (EU) Commission because there are still malters who need licences," said Alain Galaski, Secretary General of industry association Euromalt.
Malsters advised the Commission that they would be needing licences for between 1.8 million tonnes and two million tonnes this year, he said.

The European Union's cereals management committee on Thursday cut back monthly malt refunds with effect from Friday (December 20) because of the high level of applications for licences, an EU official said on Monday.
"The British government position is that more licences are needed at a proper refund rate," the official said.
The official said that a sudden rush of applications for licences leading to the award of 400,000 tonnes on Thursday was due to uncertainty about the Commission's intentions on the level of refunds.

"There was a sudden surge of applications which has taken the level of licences to the normal annual level. It is to be hoped that the Commission will restore refunds as there is still a need," the official said.
On Thursday refunds were cut significantly and the Commission indicated that it might not restore them in January.
